idiom_name: struct of creation function pointers per family (hand-rolled vtable)
implementation_notes: C has no classes, so the abstract factory becomes a struct whose members are creation function pointers, one per product kind: the struct instance is the factory, and a concrete factory is a static const struct initialized with the family's constructor functions. Each product is itself a struct whose operation pointers form its interface, following the same convention the Linux kernel uses when it installs 'a set of file operation member functions' into struct file. Return malloc'd or caller-provided pointers and document ownership (who frees) as part of the factory contract; because struct layout is the ABI, a factory struct that crosses a module or plugin boundary must be versioned or extended only by appending members. A registration table (family name → factory struct) lets the composition root select by string key without branching code.
pitfalls: No implicit this pointer: every creation function must take the factory context or product instance explicitly, or the family cannot carry configuration (connection string, theme data).
Returned pointers have no ownership contract: an undocumented malloc/free split leaks memory or double-frees products; a documented destroy function per product is usually needed.
A partially filled factory struct (NULL members) fails only when the client calls the missing operation - validate the struct at construction or keep every member non-NULL by convention.
Struct layout is the interface across translation units and shared libraries: reordering or removing function-pointer members silently breaks ABI compatibility.
A factory struct holding a void* context pointer can outlive that context if the factory is cached; validate or null the pointer when the context is destroyed.
